lot on the bottom floor of the parking garage toward the mall. the pedestrian stated the unit 1 honked their horn at them, so they stopped in between two rows of parked car. after stopping the pedestrian stated unit 1 continued to honk their horn before letting go of the brake and accelerating toward them, causing unit 1 to strike the pedestrian in their left leg the pedestrian stated that when unit 1 hit their leg, they felt a lot of pressure build up and heard a ""pop"" around their knee. unit 1 then fled the scene without stopping to provide medical attention to the pedestrian or wait for the arrival of the police. the pedestrian was able to get a picture of the driver and the license plate of the suspect vehicle. the driver of the suspect vehicle was contacted by phone, and positively identified to be the driver of unit 1 via a drivers license photograph. the driver of unit 1 stated she remembered the pedestrian walking in the parking garage and honked to get the pedestrian to move out of the traveled portion of the parking garage between two rows of parked cars. the driver went on to state that the pedestrian stopped, turned, and kicked her car while flicking her off after hearing her honk her horn. the driver stated at this point she drove around the pedestrian and stated she didn't realize she hit the pedestrian, otherwise she would have stopped. this officer was able to view security footage of the incident, and in this officers opinion the footage shows the pedestrian and unit 1 in close proximity before unit 1 drove off, possibly after striking the pedestrian . it should be noted a offense report was generated about this call (cfs: 19134194) where associated photographs and video's have been attached as evidence. in this officers opinion, unit 1 caused the crash by failing to yield right of way to a pedestrian in a parking lot. it should be noted that medics were summoned to the scene where the pedestrian was treated, [medical facility].

records.public_safe_text: unit 2 had spun out and hit the wall in a previous accident which left it facing northbound in the southbound lanes on [roadway] of 1000 n i35e sb. unit 1 was traveling southbound in the 1000 block of n 135e sb when it hit a patch of standing water causing it to hydroplane. unit 3 was in front of unit 1 traveling southbound in the 1000 block of n 135e sb. as unit 1 was hydroplaning out of control the front bumper of unit 1 collided with the rear bumper of unit 3, causing unit 3 to lose control and spin out as well. unit 3 spun [roadway] into the grassy shoulder where it came to rest facing northbound. unit 1 continued to spin out of control and crossed over to the right shoulder while traveling sideways. the driver's door of unit 1 collided with the front right front bumper of unit 2 causing damage and injury to the driver of unit 2. monica mixon was standing on the drivers side of unit 2 when unit 1 collided with it, causing unit 2 to lurch backwards into the concrete wall and pinning mixon between unit 2 and the concrete barrier. mixon was injured and required transport. ozzie williams was standing in bed of unit 2 when unit 1 collided with it, causing unit 2 to lurch backwards into the concrete wall. this caused williams to fall in the bed of unit 2 causing injury. williams required transport. mixon contacted officer o'hare in reference to the crash report and provided new information which was in contrast to some of the information collected on scene. the crash report has been amended to reflect what officer o'hare believes occured based off of this new information. mixon was contacted by email and asked to provide a written statement with her version to the lewisville police report to be included in the crash report.
